So basically since TAILS is a privacy related tool its rather important to make sure nobody has modified the files to add in a backdoor or whatever. You can uses these strings of numbers/letters to check the ISO's you download to verify they are the same ones that are official.

Now its important for every piece of software of coarse but in a case like this it is even more important I would say. Think of these patterns as a fingerprint that is unique to that exact file. What if an agency was to intercept the download and send you a modified one or somehow change the iso on the server without anyone noticing then hundreds of people could be effected. With these you can be secure in the knowledge that you have the exact one you wanted.

You need a piece of software to compare your file/iso/whatever against these numbers to verify.

The page linked has more info check out step 3.

BT Info hash is a bittorrent info-hash value - each .torrent file has one and it is used for DHT search. Same file or directory could produce different info-hashes depending on the .torrent file creation parameters. On the other hand, checksums (MD5, SHA1 and SHA256) depend solely on the file contents and would produce the same checksum for the same (byte-to-byte) file. MD5, SHA1 and SHA256 are given for the .iso file (tails-i386-1.5.iso). There is only SHA256 sum on the official website, sha1 and md5 are provided for the convenience.

Tails or The Amnesic Incognito Live System is a security-focused Debian-based Linux distribution aimed at preserving privacy and anonymity.

If something happens and the website would become unavailable, info-hash could be used to create magnet link for the bittorrent client. I posted this information as a backup for the original page. Also, Tails urges to check both SHA256 and tails-i386-1.5.iso.sig (gpg signature, file is downloaded by the torrent client).
